ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The Five Ranks of ruler and minister are a Caodong classification using sovereign and subject relations to articulate five named positions.
EvidenceBody: The Human and Celestial Eyes introduces Caoshan's explanation of the five and gives upright, biased, coming, and combined relations. Later Caodong writers compare this family with the upright-biased Five Ranks, merit ranks, and prince ranks.

Yongjue Yuanxian explicitly rejects mechanically mapping all those systems onto one five-position diagram. Juelang Daosheng likewise criticizes treating ruler and minister as mere school furniture without their active relation.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: Political offices become an interview and classification vocabulary for reciprocal position, then a subject of internal textual correction.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The entry does not collapse every Caodong fivefold system into this one; the sources themselves forbid that mapping.

ModifierControls.Finding: The defining source explicitly assigns ruler and minister relations; the political pair is not decorative.
